| INV-0001 | HW | V0 | The initial supported platform is x86-64 desktop and laptop hardware only; no other architecture is a 1.0 requirement. |
| INV-0002 | KRN | V0 | Decide the kernel strategy as a radical fork of the Linux kernel (ADR: fork vs new microkernel vs Linux-as-hypervisor), recording the rationale of hardware maturity vs native model. |
| INV-0003 | ABI | V0 | The native model must be capability-based, component-oriented, asynchronous and object-based; every native ABI surface is checked against these four properties. |
| INV-0004 | LNX | V0 | Provide a Linux/POSIX compatibility personality that runs existing Linux software. |
| INV-0005 | WIN | V2 | Provide a Windows/Win32 compatibility personality that runs existing Windows software. |
| INV-0006 | BLD | V0 | Decide the language policy: Rust for all new kernel and platform code, C retained only where inherited Linux code remains appropriate (ADR with criteria for when a C subsystem may be rewritten). |
| INV-0007 | BLD | V0 | Establish Rust-in-kernel build support (toolchain, bindings, Kbuild integration) so native kernel subsystems can be written in Rust from V0. |
| INV-0008 | GOV | V0 | Do not build another Linux distribution; the project identity and gating must reject distribution-style deliverables. |
| INV-0009 | GOV | V0 | Do not build another desktop environment on top of an existing Linux userspace. |
| INV-0010 | ABI | V0 | Do not build a Linux userspace with prettier APIs; native APIs must not be thin wrappers over Linux syscalls. |
